author: OpenAI
description:
John gave GPT-6 Astra a moonshot: design the flight-control experience for a new personal aircraft.

The gap between generating an interface and designing a system is massive, and AI models have always fallen short.

Until now.

Astra reasoned through the audience, jobs to be done, pilot-versus-passenger tradeoffs, and critical interface states. Then it connected that thinking to a real design system via the Figma MCP Server to create a polished, on-brand prototype of the concept.
title: Figma Gave GPT-6 Astra a Moonshot. Here's what happened.

author: OpenAI
description:
Veeral gave GPT-6 Astra a one-line feature request: add routing controls for individual API keys. Astra found the right settings, made the changes, and used computer use to check its own work. It verified the mobile experience without being asked.

About 12 minutes of implementing. 

Another 15 for validating.

Veeral told Romain Huet that was the shift: give Astra a high-level goal, let it make progress, and come back to changes you can review. 

We're making moves. This is why Astra is the next generation in intelligence at work.
title: One Prompt. A Feature Built and Tested. | Ramp × GPT-6 Astra

author: OpenAI
description:
Don’t sleep on Astra. Quinn Johnson started working with GPT-6 Astra differently in Codex: he shared the goal, added context, and let it tackle the problem his team had been working on. On a cache-reuse audit, Astra connected patterns the Notion team had overlooked, then explained the issue clearly. 

The Notion issue was sneaky: older messages were being regenerated using what the agent knew, subtly changing the prompt history and breaking cache reuse. 

Everything could still appear to work while becoming quietly slower and more expensive at scale.  🚀 Astra finding that hidden pattern made it a meaningful engineering win.
title: “A Staff Engineer Collaborator” | Notion’s First Look at GPT-6 Astra

author: OpenAI
description:
“How do we save time and effort and energy for our clients?”

For David Wang, Cooley’s Chief Innovation Officer, that question is central to IPO preparation, when information requests, drafting sessions, and reviews place heavy demands on senior executives.

With GO Public, built on OpenAI technology, Cooley can get substantive work in front of clients sooner and spot issues earlier. People remain responsible for reviewing the output and standing behind the answers.
title: “A Jaw Drop. Literally.” How Cooley Is Reimagining IPOs with OpenAI

author: OpenAI
description:
A 20% incentive, counted twice, could throw off an entire cost analysis. Astra caught it. Yashodha Bhavnani (Box) gave GPT-6 Astra profit, cost, and tax-incentive files to work through. It recognized that one incentive was already included, and knew to leave it alone.

Her first impression? “It blew me away.”

Watch Yash in convo with Romain Huet, as they talk about what makes Astra different and what it means for customers working with their most complex content. 

Spoiler alert: Astra excels.
title: “It Blew Me Away” | Box’s First Look at GPT-6 Astra
